Port BOTH upstream fixes with their selftest sections, localising refs per convention:
1. the quote-escape fix (objectstack PR #10406, this card);
2. the comment-rule fix (objectstack PR #11129, #5712) — merged upstream 2026-08-22.

Per-member independent check: each port's selftest section. **Exclusion list (gate ⑤)**: do NOT port the two fail-open siblings recorded in #11129's out-of-scope note (upstream objectstack#11131 backslash-desync, objectstack#11133 heredoc-in-comment) — both are unadjudicated upstream; porting them would be inventing fixes ahead of the source repo. Governed surface (`.claude/**`): draft PR, human merge, review request os-zhuang. The card's "is case-for-case identity worth a gate" question: note it in the PR body as a follow-up candidate, do not build the gate in this PR.

## Blocker verified cleared, not assumed

This card carries `Blocked-by: objectstack-ai/objectstack#10247` and the instruction "port only after that PR merges". Measured now: **objectstack#10247 is CLOSED (`completed`, 2026-08-21T00:48:21Z)**.

## Fold decision — five gates, answered

Folding #5712 in rather than serialising, because both are the same act on the same file and #5712's own title says to port it *alongside* this card:

1. **Same defect shape, same fix** — both are "this repo's copy of a deliberately-identical hook has drifted; port the upstream parsing fix". Not merely the same subsystem.
2. **Same region** — one file plus its selftest; one worktree, one queue position. `.claude/**` is not a released package, so no changeset is implicated.
3. **Both graded** — both `pm:queue` before this write; ⛔ neither is in the decision inbox.
4. **Each independently checkable** — two distinct selftest assertions, one per member (below).
5. **Exclusion list** — ⛔ NOT in scope, and each for a stated reason: `guard-main-checkout.sh` (the Edit/Write guard parses no shell text — objectstack#10247's own scope note says so), `guard-shared-stash.sh` and its selftest (a different guard; neither card claims drift there), and **objectstack's copy** (this port runs one direction only; the upstream is already fixed).

## Drift measured on `origin/main` of both repos, this round

| reading | objectstack | objectui |
|:--|--:|--:|
| `guard-main-checkout-bash.sh` line count | 505 | 433 |
| lines differing (`diff -u`) | \-- | **120** |
| comment-rule fix markers (PR #11129, = #5712) | 10 | **0** |
| backslash-in-double-quote markers (PR #10406, = this card) | 3 | 1 |

The header in both copies claims they are "deliberately kept case-for-case identical … so the two repos' guards cannot drift". They have.

⚠️ **Governed surface.** `.claude/**` is on the governed register, cross-repo. The delivering PR stays **draft**, gets `os-zhuang` requested as reviewer, and is ⛔ never flipped ready, never enqueued, never auto-merged — the maintainer's merge is the review record.

> **Exclusion list (gate ⑤)**: do NOT port the two fail-open siblings recorded in #11129's out-of-scope note (upstream objectstack#11131 backslash-desync, objectstack#11133 heredoc-in-comment) — both are unadjudicated upstream; porting them would be inventing fixes ahead of the source repo.

> The card's "is case-for-case identity worth a gate" question: note it in the PR body as a follow-up candidate, do not build the gate in this PR.

So the full exclusion list is my three (`guard-main-checkout.sh`, the stash guard pair, objectstack's own copy) **plus** those two upstream-unadjudicated fixes **plus** the identity gate itself. The dev's order carries all six.

That triage comment also independently performed the same unlock double-check I did and reached the same reading (#10247 closed completed 2026-08-21, no newer merged PR on this card) — recorded because two independent measurements agreeing is worth more than one.

## The claim I would not take on trust, re-measured

The port's central assertion is *"the residual diff against objectstack's copy is now localisation only — every logic line byte-identical."* Verified independently by fetching this PR's head and diffing against `objectstack/origin/main`:

- **Logic lines: zero difference.** The single non-comment hunk that does differ is the guard's user-facing block **message** — prose living in a string rather than behind a `#` — and it differs only by an issue reference (`#5790` → `objectui#3435`) and the re-wrap that reference forces.
- **56 differing comment lines, all localisation**: `objectstack#`-prefixed issue refs, the example path (`packages/spec/src/x.ts` → `packages/fields/src/x.tsx`), the non-ASCII example (objectstack's CLI banner `➜` → this repo's `→` in AGENTS.md, which is correct — the banner glyph does not exist here), and the provenance paragraph each copy needs for the other.
- Line counts 505 vs 501, consistent with exactly those provenance differences.

**The deliberate non-divergence is confirmed present**: both copies now read `Three layers:` above **four** enumerated layers. Ported verbatim rather than corrected, which I agree with — case-for-case identity is this file pair's whole invariant, and correcting downstream first would invent a fix ahead of the source. objectstack#11234 carries it upstream.

## What actually earns the green here

Not the `100 passed, 0 failed` — a self-test that grew by 30 cases in the same PR that fixed the code can pass without either fix being load-bearing. The **ablation** is the evidence: each fix reverted alone, the mutation proven **on disk by marker count before any result was read**, and each ablation failing **only in its own section** (4 in the `\"` section / 4 in the COMMENT section, the other section green both times). That is what makes the two members independently checkable rather than one shared assertion covering both.

Two pins I read directly in the diff and consider the load-bearing ones:

- `expect block 'sed -i "s/\"a\"/\"b\"/" pkg/x.ts'` — the **real write this guard exists to catch, which this repo's copy previously ALLOWED**. This PR is not tidiness; the shared checkout was genuinely unguarded against that shape.
- `expect block 'echo ${#TOK[@]} > pkg/x.ts'` — proves the new comment-skip cannot swallow a line and drop a real redirect behind it. Without this the comment fix would be a fail-open trade.

The `70 → 82 → 100` progression matching upstream PR #11129's own recorded `82 → 100` is independent evidence the split landed on the right line.

## ⛔ Governed surface — terminal treatment, not a landing

`.claude/**`, so the four-part treatment applies and **this PR is not being released by me**:

1. Review conclusion recorded here (cannot merge ≠ not reviewed).
2. **PR stays draft.** ⛔ Not flipped ready, not enqueued, no auto-merge. The maintainer's manual merge is the review record.
3. Review request — **could not be set, and this is a real gap, not a slip.** `Review cannot be requested from pull request author`: every agent shares the `os-zhuang` identity, so the reviewer the rule names is also the author. Already a known finding — **objectstack#11083** records exactly this. ⛔ Not re-tested here and ⛔ not worked around; nothing was flipped, relabelled or reassigned to force it. **Consequence worth stating plainly: the maintainer's push-notification channel for governed PRs does not fire for any agent-authored PR, so the round report is currently the only channel.** This PR is listed there.
4. Carried in this round's report under *awaiting a human merge*.

## Reviewer tier, declared rather than assumed

Machine reading, not self-report: `get_session` → `last_served_model: claude-opus-5`. That is **below the contract-review tier**, which the governed/skills-surface review clause asks for on a governance-surface change built at `opus`. Recording it so the maintainer can decide whether an additional top-tier review is wanted before merging. It does not gate anything today: the PR cannot merge without a human either way, and no `needs:contract-review` label is implicated (this diff touches no contract surface and the claim declared `Clause-②: no`, which the diff bears out — two shell scripts, no schema).

CI at review time: `mergeable_state: unstable`, checks still converging, **zero failures**. Tracked to green before the maintainer is asked to merge.

## What is owed by whom now

⛔ **This seat stops here.** The PR is on the governed register (`.claude/**`), so it stays **draft**, unenqueued, with no auto-merge — the maintainer's manual merge is the review record and this seat does not perform any part of it.

**@os-zhuang — the merge is yours, and note it needs the draft flip first.** GitHub will not merge a draft, and that flip is deliberately left to you rather than done here: doing it would put the PR one click from landing through a queue whose required set does not cover the gates that actually verify this change.

⚠️ **You are unlikely to have been notified.** The governed-surface rule routes "awaiting a human merge" through a review request, and that request **cannot be created** for this PR — GitHub refuses a review request from the PR's own author, and every agent shares the `os-zhuang` identity (known: objectstack#11083). So the Review-requested queue is empty by construction for agent PRs, no push fires, and this card plus the round report are the only signals that this is waiting.
